title: Experience Augmented Policy Optimization for LLM Reasoning
claim: Training from scratch is slow; injecting experience from a prior optimized policy at key decision points speeds learning and improves final accuracy.
layout: 3 panels: stacked cartoon schematics (a),(b) at left, two line plots at right
description: The figure has three dashed-border panels. At top left, panel (a) shows a cartoon robot (π_Base) passing through a teal circular-arrows RL icon to become a armored, arms-crossed robot (π_RL). A grey down arrow leads to panel (b), where the base robot sits at left and the armored π_RL robot at right. Between them, a dashed blue trajectory has vertical arrows dropping onto a lower baseline path, with glowing nodes marking critical decision points where experience is injected. Panel (c) on the right holds two line plots of AIME'24 Mean@32 against training steps, for Qwen-2.5-7B Math and Qwen-3-8B Base. Dark blue is baseline DAPO. Two red lines are EAPO runs. The red lines climb faster and end higher, and a black box highlights the late-training gap.
caption: Overview of experience-augmented reinforcement learning. (a) Standard reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) optimizes a base policy $\pi_{Base}$ into an RL-optimized policy $\pi_{RL}$ through iterative rollouts and policy updates. (b) Instead of training from scratch, EAPO leverages experience from a prior RL-optimized policy $\pi_{RL}$ during rollout of the current policy by resampling actions at critical decision points, introducing experience that adapts to the evolving policy. (c) Empirical comparisons on AIME'24 show that incorporating experience from $\pi_{RL}$ significantly accelerates exploration and improves accuracy compared to DAPO [ref], across various base models (Qwen-2.5-7B-Math [ref] and Qwen-3-8B [ref]).
abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, existing RLVR methods typically rely on on-policy optimization from scratch, resulting in high sampling costs and inefficient utilization of accumulated experience. As model capabilities and policy behaviors evolve during training, recent attempts to reuse experience via fixed reasoning trajectories further suffer from policy mismatch. Motivated by these limitations, we argue that experience in RLVR should not be reused as fixed reasoning trajectories, but instead expressed in a policy-adaptive manner. In this work, we propose Experience-Augmented Policy Optimization (EAPO), which leverages a prior RL-optimized policy as an action-level experience prior and selectively injects experience at critical decision points during rollout. To ensure stable and unbiased learning from experience-augmented rollouts, EAPO further incorporates an adapted importance sampling scheme. Experiments on using Qwen-2.5-math 7b and Qwen-3-8B on five different benchmarks demonstrate that EAPO consistently improves reasoning performance over state-of-the-art RLVR methods.
